item.title: Tokyo National Museum — Guide
item.description: The Tokyo National Museum (Tokyo Kokuritsu Hakubutsukan), founded in 1872 and set in Ueno Park, is Japan’s oldest and largest museum, and home to the world’s most comprehensive collection of Japanese art and archaeology. Its vast holdings — over 110,000 items including scores of designated National Treasures and Important Cultural Properties — span the whole sweep of Japanese culture: samurai swords and armour, exquisite Buddhist sculpture, painted screens and scrolls, ceramics, lacquerware, ukiyo-e woodblock prints, kimono and textiles, and archaeological finds.
